merger_description:
Cerberus Capital Management, L.P. (**Cerberus**), through funds advised and managed by its affiliates, proposes to acquire the high integrity products, radar systems and submersible pumps businesses (**Mechanical Engineering Business**) of Goodwin PLC (**Goodwin**) as part of a global transaction (the **Acquisition**).

Cerberus is a global alternative investment firm headquartered in New York. It has approximately USD 72 billion of assets under management globally across various sectors.

Prior to completion, Goodwin is undertaking an internal reorganisation to transfer the assets and operations of the Mechanical Engineering Business to Lord Holdco Limited, a new legal entity established for the Acquisition.

Goodwin is a group of mechanical and refractory engineering companies listed on the London Stock Exchange. In Australia, Goodwin supplies a range of pumps, radar parts, steel components and specialist valve products, including through the following Australian entities:

* Goodwin Submersible Pumps Australia Pty Ltd (**GSPA**): a wholly owned Australian subsidiary of Goodwin. GSPA supplies submersible slurry pumps manufactured by Goodwin to Australian customers.
* Easat Radar Systems Ltd: supplies radar spare parts.
* Goodwin International Limited: supplies dual plate and axial check valves.
* Noreva GmbH: supplies check and control valves.
* Goodwin Steel Castings Limited: supplies high-integrity case and machined steel components.

Cerberus and its portfolio companies are not active in the supply of these products or related markets.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver and had regard
to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationships between the parties (or their connected
entities).
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
